## Product Analytics Transition Snapshot

You already have a strong technical base for product analytics: backend experience, data thinking, and likely comfort with SQL, APIs, and experimentation support. The biggest gap is usually not “analytics math” but translating product behavior into decisions, metrics, and stakeholder-ready insights.

## Skill-Gap Analysis and 12-Week Plan

| Area | Current Advantage | Gap to Close | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| SQL & data modeling | Likely strong query discipline from backend work | Window functions, cohort analysis, funnels, retention, metric definitions | High |
| Product analytics tools | Familiar with systems and data flows | Amplitude/Mixpanel/GA4 event design and dashboards | High |
| Experimentation | Can understand implementation details | A/B test design, guardrails, statistical interpretation | High |
| Business thinking | Can reason about systems and tradeoffs | Product metrics, north-star metrics, KPI trees, decision framing | High |
| Communication | Technical explanations likely solid | Turning analyses into concise recommendations for PMs | High |
| Portfolio evidence | Can build systems | Need public or shareable case studies showing product impact | Medium |
| Domain fluency | Backend context is valuable | Product lifecycle, activation, retention, monetization language | Medium |

### 12-Week Learning Plan

| Week | Focus | Key Work | Deliverable |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Product analytics foundations | Learn funnel, cohort, retention, activation, LTV, CAC; map metrics to product goals | One-page metric glossary |
| 2 | SQL for analytics | Practice joins, CTEs, window functions, segmentation, date logic | 15–20 solved SQL problems |
| 3 | Funnel analysis | Build a funnel from raw event data; identify drop-offs and hypotheses | Funnel analysis write-up |
| 4 | Retention and cohorts | Create cohort tables, retention curves, and churn views | Cohort dashboard mockup |
| 5 | Event tracking design | Define events, properties, naming conventions, and data quality checks | Tracking plan for one product flow |
| 6 | Experimentation basics | Learn hypothesis setup, sample size intuition, p-values, guardrails | A/B test analysis memo |
| 7 | Dashboarding | Build KPI dashboard in Looker Studio, Tableau, or Metabase | Metrics dashboard project |
| 8 | Product case studies | Analyze a product feature, onboarding flow, or pricing page | 1 polished case study |
| 9 | Stakeholder communication | Practice writing concise insight-to-action summaries | 3 executive-style insight memos |
| 10 | Portfolio packaging | Clean up projects, screenshots, and narrative | Portfolio page or Notion doc |
| 11 | Résumé and LinkedIn | Reframe backend experience toward metrics, experimentation, and product impact | Updated résumé and profile |
| 12 | Interview prep | Practice product sense, SQL, analytics, and behavioral stories | Mock interview packet |

### Realistic 6-Month Positioning

- **Best-fit target roles:** Product Analyst, Growth Analyst, Analytics Engineer with product exposure, Business/Product Data Analyst.
- **Salary target realism in Mexico City:** **MXN 70,000+ monthly** is achievable, but more realistic if you target:
  - multinational tech companies
  - fintech, SaaS, marketplaces, and growth-stage startups
  - roles that value SQL plus experimentation and dashboard ownership
- **Likely hiring signal:** your backend background becomes a plus if you can show:
  - event instrumentation understanding
  - SQL-driven insights
  - product metric ownership
  - experimentation or decision support

### Résumé Bullet Examples

- Built SQL-based funnel and retention analyses for a backend-powered product, identifying a 12% drop-off point in onboarding and recommending instrumentation and UX changes that improved activation tracking.
- Partnered with product and engineering teams to define event schemas, tracking requirements, and data quality checks, enabling reliable self-serve reporting for core product KPIs.
- Designed and analyzed A/B test readouts for feature releases, translating results into clear recommendations on rollout strategy, user impact, and metric guardrails.
